slot.brief: Convert a phenol to anisole-like ether in 2–3 steps; identify correct reagent sequence (NaOH, CH3I/Williamson, etc.).

stem: The correct sequence of reagents for converting phenol to anisole is:

verdicts.working: NaOH deprotonates phenol to form phenoxide; phenoxide reacts with CH₃I to form anisole by O-methylation.

working:
Phenol is deprotonated by NaOH to form the reactive phenoxide ion; subsequent SN2 reaction with methyl iodide (CH₃I) gives anisole (Williamson ether synthesis).

Independent check: NaOH deprotonates phenol to form phenoxide; phenoxide reacts with CH₃I to form anisole by O-methylation.
solution:
NaOH deprotonates phenol to form phenoxide, which undergoes $S_N2$ O-methylation with methyl iodide.
$$\mathrm{C_6H_5OH \xrightarrow{NaOH} C_6H_5O^- \xrightarrow{CH_3I} C_6H_5OCH_3}$$
